body.back: A business owned by two to twenty people who agree to share capital, profits, losses and responsibilities, usually set out in a partnership agreement.
Profit-sharing ratio, interest on capital, interest on drawings, partners' salaries, capital contributed by each partner (any two).
body.front: Name two items usually included in a partnership agreement.

body.back: More capital can be raised; shared workload and skills; risks and decisions are shared between partners (any one).
body.front: State one advantage of a partnership over a sole trader.
body.hint: More people, more money and skills.

body.back: Partners have unlimited liability; profits must be shared; disagreements may occur; one partner's decisions bind all partners (any one).
body.front: State one disadvantage of a partnership.
body.hint: Unlimited liability = personal assets at risk.

body.back: Partners are personally responsible for all the debts of the business, so their personal assets may be used to pay them.
To show how the net profit is shared between partners, after adjusting for salaries, interest on capital and interest on drawings.
body.front: What is the purpose of a partnership appropriation account?

body.back: A reward paid to partners for the capital they have invested in the business, calculated as a percentage of their capital.
A charge made to partners for cash or goods taken from the business for personal use, discouraging excessive drawings.
body.hint: Charged to partner, so it increases profit to share.

body.back: An agreed amount paid to a partner for work done in the business, treated as an appropriation of profit, not an expense.
body.hint: Salary is in appropriation, not the income statement.

body.back: Under the Partnership Act, profits and losses are shared equally, with no interest on capital, no interest on drawings and no salaries.
body.front: What happens if there is no partnership agreement?
body.hint: No agreement = equal shares, no extras.

body.back: Capital account records the fixed capital invested; current account records the share of profit, interest, salaries and drawings, and fluctuates each year.
body.front: Difference between a capital account and a current account?

body.back: Drawings are entered on the debit side of the partner's current account, reducing the balance.
body.front: How are drawings recorded in the partners' current accounts?

body.back: On the credit side of the partner's current account, increasing the balance.
body.front: Where are profit share, salary and interest on capital entered in the current account?

body.back: The partner's drawings and interest on drawings are greater than their share of profit, salary and interest on capital.
body.front: Why might a partner's current account have a debit balance?

body.back: In the capital employed (equity) section, with each partner's capital and current account balances shown separately.
body.front: Where are partners' capital and current accounts shown in the statement of financial position?
